title: The Day the Locks Stopped Working
Banking: The SWIFT Collapse
story: A ghost in the machine transferring billions.

caseStudy.background: The SWIFT network handles trillions in daily cross-border transfers. It relies heavily on RSA/ECC for digital signatures to verify the authenticity of payment instructions.
caseStudy.technicalRisk: A cryptographically relevant quantum computer could forge these signatures in seconds, allowing an attacker to inject fake 'High-Value' payment messages that appear perfectly legitimate.
caseStudy.mitigation: Implementation of Hash-based signatures (LMS/XMSS) for message integrity and Lattice-based KEMs for session key exchange.
caseStudy.experimentSetup: A simulated banking environment using a 'Quantum Adversary' module that attempts to sign transaction headers using Shor's algorithm emulation.
caseStudy.insight: Post-Quantum migration for banking is not just about secrecy, but about preventing a global liquidity freeze caused by loss of trust.

title: Healthcare: The Genomic Leak
story: Your DNA is a permanent password that can't be changed.

caseStudy.background: Hospitals store patient genomic data (DNA) for personalized medicine. This data remains sensitive for the patient's entire life and across generations.
caseStudy.technicalRisk: SNDL (Store Now, Decrypt Later). Adversaries are harvesting genomic databases today, waiting for Q-Day to unlock them. Once leaked, DNA data cannot be 'reset' like a password.
caseStudy.mitigation: Retroactive encryption using AES-256 for storage and transitioning to ML-KEM (Kyber) for all data-in-transit by 2026.
caseStudy.experimentSetup: Entropy analysis of encrypted genomic sequences to verify that PQC-wrapped data shows zero correlation even under quantum-level heat maps.
caseStudy.insight: In healthcare, 'Future Proofing' is a legal and ethical mandate, as a breach in 2035 exposes a child's future in 2090.

title: Energy: Grid Lockdown
story: A city goes dark because its meters were tricked into 'Sleep' mode.

caseStudy.background: Modern power grids use automated SCADA systems and billions of IoT smart meters to balance load. These devices use light-weight crypto to verify firmware updates.
caseStudy.technicalRisk: Quantum computers can forge firmware signatures, allowing an attacker to send a 'Kill' command or malicious firmware to every smart meter in a country simultaneously.
caseStudy.mitigation: Upgrading to stateless PQC signatures (Dilithium/ML-DSA) for secure boot and firmware-over-the-air (FOTA) updates.
caseStudy.experimentSetup: A hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) testbed where a simulated quantum attacker tries to bypass a smart meter's secure boot sequence.
caseStudy.insight: The grid's biggest vulnerability is the long lifecycle of IoT hardware; we must build 'PQC-Ready' hardware today for devices that will last 20 years.

title: Gov: The Satellite Hijack
story: A billion-dollar satellite receiving commands from an unknown source.
enterpriseInsight: Command and control must be quantum-proof.

caseStudy.background: Global navigation and communication satellites (GNSS/SATCOM) use encrypted telemetry for orbital maintenance and command relay.
caseStudy.technicalRisk: Command-and-Control (C2) links are often protected by legacy asymmetric protocols. A quantum adversary could hijack a satellite's thrusters by breaking the C2 handshake.
caseStudy.mitigation: Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) for ground-to-space links and Lattice-based signatures for command authentication.
caseStudy.experimentSetup: Simulation of a Doppler-shifted communication link subjected to a 'Man-in-the-Middle' quantum attack on the key exchange phase.
caseStudy.insight: Space security is the ultimate high-ground; losing a satellite to quantum forgery is a permanent and expensive defeat.

title: Auto: The V2V Breach
story: Cars talking to each other, but one is a liar.

caseStudy.background: Vehicle-to-Vehicle (V2V) and V2X communication allows autonomous cars to share speed and location to prevent collisions.
caseStudy.technicalRisk: Short-range certificates (IEEE 1609.2) rely on ECDSA. A quantum computer could generate fake 'Emergency Braking' signals for every car in a 10-mile radius, causing mass pileups.
caseStudy.mitigation: Transitioning to Falcon or Dilithium for certificate signing, optimized for the low-latency requirements of automotive safety.
caseStudy.experimentSetup: Traffic simulation where 'ghost' vehicles (quantum forgeries) attempt to force human-operated and AI vehicles into collision paths.
caseStudy.insight: In V2X, 'Trust-at-Speed' is essential. PQC signatures must be fast enough to be verified within milliseconds to maintain safety.

title: Pharma: The Formula Theft
story: A decade of research walking out the back door in an encrypted file that will soon be cleartext.
enterpriseInsight: IP value is tied to its secrecy duration.

caseStudy.background: Pharmaceutical companies spend billions on R&D for new drugs. These formulas are stored in highly secure, encrypted R&D vaults.
caseStudy.technicalRisk: The 'Harvest Now, Decrypt Later' threat is acute here. Foreign intelligence captures encrypted R&D data in 2024, expecting to decrypt the 'Billion Dollar Molecule' by 2030.
caseStudy.mitigation: Immediate re-encryption of all 'Crown Jewel' IP with AES-256 and wrapping data-at-rest in PQC-based digital envelopes.
caseStudy.experimentSetup: A 'Time-Lock' simulation where encrypted lab data is evaluated for its vulnerability over a 5, 10, and 15-year horizon.
caseStudy.insight: PQC is not an IT cost for Pharma; it is an Asset Protection strategy to preserve the ROI of multi-year clinical trials.

title: Cloud: The Hypervisor Breach
story: The walls between your data and your competitor's data just turned into glass.
enterpriseInsight: Isolation is an illusion without crypto.

caseStudy.background: Cloud providers (AWS/Azure/GCP) use virtualization to isolate data between different companies sharing the same physical hardware.
caseStudy.technicalRisk: The 'Root of Trust' for the cloud hypervisor relies on hardware security modules (HSMs). If the HSM's RSA/ECC keys are broken, an attacker can move laterally between any company's data.
caseStudy.mitigation: Implementing Hardware-based PQC (Quantum-Safe HSMs) and multi-factor PQC authentication for administrative access.
caseStudy.experimentSetup: A 'Blue Team vs Quantum Red Team' exercise where the attacker attempts to extract tenant-level keys using a simulated quantum side-channel.
caseStudy.insight: Cloud customers must demand 'Quantum Transparency' from their providers—knowing exactly which layers are PQC-protected.

title: Retail: The Digital Identity Theft
story: Someone buying a yacht using your face and your digital wallet.

caseStudy.background: E-commerce and Retail giants use digital identities (SAML/OIDC) and biometrics for 'One-Click' payments and account access.
caseStudy.technicalRisk: The digital certificates that vouch for your identity are vulnerable. A quantum attacker could forge a 'Master Identity' that passes all biometric and cryptographic checks.
caseStudy.mitigation: Upgrading FIDO2/WebAuthn keys to include PQC-resistant algorithms and using hybrid signatures for all transaction receipts.
caseStudy.experimentSetup: An identity-provider (IdP) test where 1 million login requests are screened for 'Quantum Signature Anomalies' using AI-driven detection.
caseStudy.insight: In a post-quantum world, 'Identity' must be reinforced by multiple, independent layers of math (Lattices + Hashes) to remain credible.

title: Defense: The Secure Burst
story: Orders from the General that never came from the General.
enterpriseInsight: Battlefield trust is won with math.

caseStudy.background: Military units use 'Burst' transmissions to send coordinates and orders. These must be encrypted and signed to prevent enemy spoofing.
caseStudy.technicalRisk: Quantum computers could break the 'Order-of-Battle' encryption in real-time, allowing an enemy to issue retreat orders to friendly troops or redirect artillery.
caseStudy.mitigation: Deployment of 'One-Time-Pad' (OTP) for critical coordinates and HQC (Hybrid-Code-based) crypto for high-bandwidth tactical data.
caseStudy.experimentSetup: A tactical radio field-test where PQC-enabled radios are subjected to 'Quantum Jamming' and 'Quantum Spoofing' attempts.
caseStudy.insight: National security is the primary driver of PQC; the first country to achieve 'Quantum Supremacy' in cryptanalysis has a temporary but absolute advantage.

title: Supply Chain: The OTA Poisoning
story: Your new phone arriving with a spy already living inside its brain.
enterpriseInsight: The chain is only as strong as its weakest link.

caseStudy.background: Global supply chains for microchips use over-the-air (OTA) updates and digital signing for firmware provenance from factory to consumer.
caseStudy.technicalRisk: Quantum forgery at the 'Root Certificate' level would allow an adversary to sign malicious microcode for an entire batch of CPUs, creating a hardware back-door.
caseStudy.mitigation: Implementing 'Double-Signing' with both Classical and PQC algorithms during the manufacturing and distribution stages.
caseStudy.experimentSetup: A supply chain audit simulation where firmware is verified using a 'Quantum-Safe Proof-of-Origin' ledger.
caseStudy.insight: Supply chain security is a 'Zero Trust' game; we must verify the math at every hop, from the silicon foundry to the end-user's hand.
